hook: 77,562 reviews say this $35 insert beats a $200 duvet

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up hand scrolling Amazon reviews on phone, 4.7 stars and '77,562 ratings' visible on screen
scenes.voiceover: I didn't believe a $34.99 comforter could have 77,562 reviews until I counted them myself.

scenes.visual_prompt: Split screen: flat, thin comforter on unmade bed vs. thick, lofted comforter on made bed
scenes.on_screen_text: This is the layer everyone skips
scenes.voiceover: Most bedding refreshes skip this part completely — they buy a comforter-in-a-bag set that flattens in a month.

scenes.visual_prompt: Product shot of Bedsure Comforter Duvet Insert package, Oeko-TEX tag close-up
scenes.voiceover: The Bedsure insert is $34.99, tested for harmful substances, and it's the piece that goes underneath the cover, not on top.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands pulling comforter insert out of washing machine, still lofted and fluffy
scenes.voiceover: Reviewers keep saying the same thing — it survives the wash. That's the actual failure point for cheap comforters.

scenes.visual_prompt: Insert being stuffed into a plain white duvet cover, corner ties visible
scenes.voiceover: If you buy this expecting to use it bare, you're missing the point. It's built to live inside a cover.

scenes.visual_prompt: Finished bed shot, plush and hotel-like, text overlay with price
scenes.on_screen_text: Queen size sells the most — for a reason
scenes.voiceover: Queen is the size that shows up most in the review data, and now I understand why.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final CTA frame, link sticker to blog post
scenes.voiceover: I broke down all five pieces of this look and what they actually cost. Link's in my bio.

caption: I was skeptical that a $34.99 insert could do anything a $200 hotel duvet couldn't — then I read all 77,562 reviews (okay, most of them). The insert is the piece nobody buys and it's the one that actually matters. Full breakdown of the 5-item stack on the blog, link in bio.
